utterance_starts.first_words: Señora senadora discúlpeme. El senador Passo le solicita una interrupción. ¿Se la concede?
Para una interrupción, tiene la palabra el señor senador Passo.
Señor presidente: intentaré hacer una contribución en un debate que comenzó verdaderamente realzado
Continúa en el uso de la palabra la señora senadora Negre de Alonso.
Señor presidente: me congratula que el señor senador a quien concedí la interrupción esté preocupado

notes: Six turns, the whole fragment being one granted interruption and the return from it. The stretch begins exactly on the chair's label, so nothing opens mid-speech, although the speech the chair interrupts (Negre de Alonso's) did begin earlier in the sitting and is therefore not listed. The one judgement call: the last entry, Negre de Alonso after 'Continúa en el uso de la palabra', is the resumption of that same earlier speech. I counted it as a start because the page prints a fresh bold label for it and two other people have spoken in between, which makes it a new labelled turn on the page even though it continues the same argument; a reader counting labels and a reader counting speeches would differ here by one. Her two-word consent turn ('Con mucho gusto, señor presidente.') is short but is a turn and is counted. All three chair labels print 'Sr. Presidente (Maqueda). --' with the name outside the first bold run and the '. --' in a second one. Every paragraph in this fragment is trailed by an empty <FONT FACE="Arial,Helvética"></FONT> run, which is a WordPerfect export artifact and prints nothing, so it is not recorded as furniture. No stenographer's notes, headings, back-links or inserted documents. The stretch ends in the middle of Negre de Alonso's speech.
